name: k6
what_it_is: k6 is a modern open-source load testing tool built by Grafana Labs that uses an embedded JavaScript/ES6 engine backed by a Go runtime, enabling developers and testers to write performance tests as code. It is designed for developer experience in DevOps workflows, supporting CLI execution, CI pipeline integration, and distributed Kubernetes-based runs.
components: JavaScript/ES6 scripting engine (Goja, Go-based JS runtime)
Scenario scheduler (open model, closed model, constant RPS, fixed iterations)
Output connectors (InfluxDB, Prometheus, Grafana Cloud, CSV, JSON, StatsD)
k6 Studio (code-free script generation companion tool)
k6 Cloud / Grafana Cloud integration for distributed runs and result analysis
measurement: Custom metrics (Counter, Gauge, Rate, Trend types)
Threshold-based pass/fail assertions on any metric
configuration: options export object in JS script (vus, duration, stages, thresholds, scenarios)
Config file (k6 run --config) for reusable option sets
fault_injection: sleep() calls in scripts to simulate think time and pacing
Custom error rate simulation via check() and deliberate bad requests
Scenario ramping (stages) to model sudden traffic spikes and drops
modes: CI pipeline integration (outputs exit codes for pass/fail)
Distributed cloud execution (Grafana Cloud k6 / k6 Cloud)
Browser performance testing mode (k6 browser module)
constraints: No built-in chaos/fault injection primitives — fault simulation must be coded manually in JS
No native database protocol support (SQL, MongoDB, Redis) in core — requires community extensions (xk6)
JavaScript execution is single-threaded per VU; CPU-bound JS logic limits achievable concurrency on a single machine
Browser module requires Chromium and significantly higher resource usage than protocol-level tests
Distributed runs beyond a single machine require Grafana Cloud k6 or self-managed Kubernetes operator — no built-in peer-to-peer coordination
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the grafana/k6 repository (404) — k6 is distributed as a standalone binary/Docker image, not a multi-service stack
No built-in result storage — requires external time-series DB (InfluxDB, Prometheus) or Grafana Cloud
No GUI in core — k6 Studio is a separate companion application
No native MQTT, AMQP, or TCP protocol support in core (available only via xk6 community extensions)
No built-in test data generation library — users must implement or import data generation in JS
